cases.sentence: Она крепче оперлась на его ___ и прижала ее к себе.
cases.translation: She leaned more firmly on his arm and pressed it to herself.
cases.explain: The preposition на (onto) with a verb of motion/pressure governs the accusative case here.

cases.sentence: Ему хотелось слышать звук ее ___, так же, как и взгляд.
cases.translation: He wanted to hear the sound of her voice, as well as her glance.
cases.explain: Звук ее голоса (the sound OF her voice) requires the possessed noun to be in the genitive case.

cases.sentence: «Сергей в этом отношении очень странен для ___», — сказала она.
cases.translation: Sergei is very strange to me in this respect.
cases.explain: The preposition для (for) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: «Но не так, как с ___ покойным. Вы полюбили друг друга», — докончил Левин.
cases.translation: But not the way it was with the late Nikolenka. You two came to love each other, Levin finished.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: «Я по ___ ничего не желаю, кроме того, чтобы вот ты не споткнулась».
cases.translation: In my heart I want nothing except that you don't stumble.
cases.explain: The expression по душе (to one's liking/in one's heart) uses the preposition по governing the dative case.

cases.sentence: Она нагнулась и сорвала на краю дороги дикую ___.
cases.translation: She bent down and picked a wild daisy at the edge of the road.
cases.explain: Ромашку is the direct object of сорвала (picked), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.translation: Here comes the carriage that has caught up with us.
cases.explain: Линейка is the subject of догнала (caught up with), so it stands in the nominative case.

reading.ru: Китти была в особенности рада случаю побыть с глазу на глаз с мужем
reading.question: Why was Kitty especially glad of the chance to be alone with her husband?
options: She had noticed a shadow of sorrow cross his face when no one answered his question
She wanted to discuss the jam recipe
She wanted to complain about her mother
She wanted to plan a trip to Moscow
reading.correct: She had noticed a shadow of sorrow cross his face when no one answered his question
reading.explain: Kitty noticed a shadow of vexation cross Levin's expressive face when his question went unanswered, and wanted to be alone with him.

reading.ru: Когда они пошли пешком вперед других и вышли из виду дома на накатанную, пыльную и усыпанную ржаными колосьями и зернами дорогу, она крепче оперлась на его руку и прижала ее к себе.
reading.question: What did Kitty do once they were out of sight of the house?
options: She leaned more firmly on his arm and pressed it to herself
reading.correct: She leaned more firmly on his arm and pressed it to herself
reading.explain: Once out of sight of the house, Kitty leaned more heavily on his arm and pressed it close to her.

reading.ru: Он уже забыл о минутном неприятном впечатлении и наедине с нею испытывал теперь
reading.question: What had Levin already forgotten as he walked alone with Kitty?
options: The momentary unpleasant impression from before
reading.correct: The momentary unpleasant impression from before
reading.explain: Levin had already forgotten the momentary unpleasant impression and was now enjoying being alone with her.

reading.ru: «Так ты не устанешь? Упирайся больше», — сказал он.
reading.question: What does Levin ask Kitty, concerned she might get tired?
options: Whether she will get tired, telling her to lean on him more
Whether she wants to turn back
Whether she wants to sit down
reading.correct: Whether she will get tired, telling her to lean on him more
reading.explain: Levin asks if she won't get tired and tells her to lean on him more.

reading.ru: «Нет, я так рада случаю побыть с тобой наедине и признаюсь, как мне нехорошо с ними, жалко наших зимних вечеров вдвоем».
reading.question: What does Kitty confess about being with the guests compared to their winter evenings alone?
options: That she finds it unpleasant with them and misses their winter evenings together
That she loves having so many guests around
That she wants more guests to visit
That she prefers summer to winter
reading.correct: That she finds it unpleasant with them and misses their winter evenings together
reading.explain: Kitty admits she feels unwell being around all the guests and misses their private winter evenings as a couple.

reading.ru: «Ты знаешь, про что мы говорили, когда ты вошел?» «Про варенье?»
reading.question: What does Levin guess the women were talking about when he entered?
reading.explain: When Kitty asks if he knows what they were discussing, Levin guesses 'about the jam?'

reading.ru: «Да, и про варенье, но потом о том, как делают предложение».
reading.question: What did the women's conversation move on to after the jam?
options: How a man makes a marriage proposal
What to name a new baby
reading.correct: How a man makes a marriage proposal
reading.explain: Kitty tells him they also talked about jam, but then moved on to how a proposal is made.

reading.ru: «И о Сергее Ивановиче и Вареньке. Ты заметил?»
reading.question: Which couple does Kitty ask Levin if he has noticed something about?
reading.explain: Kitty asks Levin whether he has noticed anything about Sergei Ivanovich and Varenka.

reading.ru: «Сергей в этом отношении очень странен для меня. Я ведь рассказывал. Да, что он был влюблен в эту девушку, которая умерла.
reading.question: What does Levin recall about his brother Sergei's past?
options: That Sergei had once been in love with a girl who died
That Sergei never wanted to marry
That Sergei was engaged once before
That Sergei disliked Varenka from the start
reading.correct: That Sergei had once been in love with a girl who died
reading.explain: Levin recalls that Sergei was once in love with a girl who died, when Levin himself was still a child.

reading.ru: «Может быть и есть, но его надо знать. Он особенный, удивительный человек, он живет одной духовной жизнью».
reading.question: How does Levin describe his brother Sergei's character?
options: A special, remarkable man who lives purely a spiritual life
A man who avoids all responsibility
reading.correct: A special, remarkable man who lives purely a spiritual life
reading.explain: Levin describes Sergei as a special, remarkable man who lives entirely a life of the spirit.

reading.ru: «Я завидую тому, что он лучше меня», — улыбаясь, сказал Левин.
reading.question: What does Levin say, smiling, that he envies about his brother?
options: That his brother is better than he is
That his brother is more handsome
That his brother has more friends
reading.correct: That his brother is better than he is
reading.explain: Levin smilingly admits he envies the fact that his brother is a better person than he is.

reading.ru: «Он живет не для себя. У него вся жизнь подчинена долгу, и потому он может быть спокоен и доволен».
reading.question: Why does Levin say Sergei can be calm and content?
options: Because his whole life is subordinated to duty rather than himself
Because he never worries about others
reading.correct: Because his whole life is subordinated to duty rather than himself
reading.explain: Levin explains that Sergei does not live for himself; his entire life is subject to duty, which lets him be calm and content.

reading.ru: «Я счастлив, но недоволен собой», — сказал он.
reading.question: What contradictory feeling does Levin admit to?
options: That he is happy but dissatisfied with himself
That he is unhappy but satisfied with himself
That he is neither happy nor unhappy
That he is angry but calm
reading.correct: That he is happy but dissatisfied with himself
reading.explain: Levin admits that although he is happy, he is dissatisfied with himself.

reading.ru: «Ах, да ведь нельзя же так прыгать!» — прервал он свой разговор упреком за то, что она сделала слишком быстрое движение, переступая через лежавший на тропинке сук.
reading.question: Why did Levin suddenly interrupt himself to scold Kitty?
options: Because she jumped too quickly over a branch on the path
Because she was walking too slowly
reading.correct: Because she jumped too quickly over a branch on the path
reading.explain: Levin broke off to reproach her for making too sudden a movement stepping over a branch on the path.

reading.ru: «Разве ты тоже не делаешь для других? И твои хутора, и твое хозяйство, и твоя книга?»
reading.question: What does Kitty point out that Levin does for others?
options: His farms, his estate management, and his book
His charity work in the village
reading.correct: His farms, his estate management, and his book
reading.explain: Kitty reminds him that he too works for others, citing his farms, his household management, and his book.

reading.ru: Она нагнулась и сорвала на краю дороги дикую ромашку.
reading.question: What did Kitty pick from the side of the road?
reading.explain: Kitty bent down and picked a wild daisy from the edge of the road.

reading.ru: «Ну, считай, сделает, не сделает предложение», — сказала она, подавая ему цветок.
reading.question: What game does Kitty suggest playing with the flower's petals?
options: A petal-counting game to predict whether Sergei will propose
A guessing game about the weather
A memory game about their wedding
A counting game about the harvest
reading.correct: A petal-counting game to predict whether Sergei will propose
reading.explain: Kitty hands him the flower and suggests they use it to count out whether he will propose or not.

reading.ru: Не устала ли ты, Китти? — прокричала княгиня.
reading.question: What does the princess call out to ask Kitty as the carriage catches up?
options: Whether she wants to go home
Whether she has seen Sergei Ivanovich
reading.explain: The princess calls out asking whether Kitty is tired.
